## Natural history notes

A small flea beetle characterized by a shiny dark body, pale yellowish legs, and enlarged hind femora that allow it to jump quickly when disturbed. In Florida, the Pale-legged Flea Beetle is found in wetlands, marsh edges, ponds, canals, ditches, and other moist habitats where aquatic or semi-aquatic host plants grow. Adults feed by chewing small holes or patches in leaves, while the larvae develop on or near host plant roots or submerged plant tissue, linking wetland vegetation to predators such as spiders, predatory bugs, birds, and small fishes.
